sources.note: Reaches test-time scaling with two simple ingredients: supervised finetuning on 1,000 curated reasoning traces, and 'budget forcing', which controls thinking length by cutting generation off or appending 'Wait' to extend it.
sources.title: s1: Simple test-time scaling

sources.note: Uses elliptical bonuses over a language model's own hidden-state representations as a diversity signal, validates it in a clean inference-time selection setting, then transfers the same signal into RL post-training — where it eliminates the diversity collapse that degrades pass@k at large k.
sources.title: Representation-Based Exploration for Language Models: From Test-Time to Post-Training

sources.note: Tracks mutual information between each reasoning step's representation and the correct answer, finds it spikes at sparse 'MI peaks' that decode to reflective tokens like 'Wait' and 'Hmm', and shows suppressing exactly those tokens degrades reasoning while suppressing equally many others does not.
sources.title: Demystifying Reasoning Dynamics with Mutual Information: Thinking Tokens are Information Peaks in LLM Reasoning

sources.note: Formalizes 'spend test-time compute well' as a meta-reinforcement-learning problem — treating one long output stream as a sequence of episodes and scoring it by cumulative regret over tokens — and trains against a dense progress bonus that outcome-only reward cannot express.
sources.title: Optimizing Test-Time Compute via Meta Reinforcement Fine-Tuning

sources.note: Introduces EDIS, a trajectory-level score that measures how unstably token entropy evolves during generation, and uses it to select better reasoning rollouts at inference and to curate training samples in RL.
sources.title: EDIS: Diagnosing LLM Reasoning via Entropy Dynamics

result.definition: The competition-mathematics benchmark, cited here in its full form rather than the 500-problem subset that appears separately in this archive. The sources use it as a mid-to-hard evaluation set: a model finetuned on 1,000 curated traces with budget forcing exceeds o1-preview by up to 27% on it together with AIME24; a hundred sampled problems serve as the inference-time selection testbed where entropy-instability filtering reaches 62.3% against 54.0% for the next-best confidence measure; and its training split is where thinking tokens are mined offline before being triggered on surface form at inference. Note that this entry and MATH500 name the same underlying benchmark at different sizes, harvested separately because the archived summaries referred to them differently.
